definitions.explanation: A flour milled from regular (non-glutinous) short-grain rice, used to make {団子|だんご}, {柏餅|かしわもち}, and other Japanese sweets that need a firm, springy texture.

examples.japanese: {上新粉|じょうしんこ}で{団子|だんご}を{作|つく}る。
examples.english: I make dango with non-glutinous rice flour.

examples.japanese: {上新粉|じょうしんこ}を{熱湯|ねっとう}でこねる。
examples.english: Knead the rice flour with boiling water.

examples.japanese: {上新粉|じょうしんこ}は{蒸|む}してからつくと、{滑|なめ}らかでこしのある{団子|だんご}になる。
examples.english: If you steam and then pound non-glutinous rice flour, you get smooth, chewy dango.

notes:
Made from うるち{米|まい} (regular short-grain rice), unlike もち{米|ごめ} (glutinous rice) which produces もち{粉|こ} and {白玉粉|しらたまこ}. Gives a firmer, chewier texture than glutinous rice flours.

SIMILAR FLOURS:
- {白玉粉|しらたまこ}: shiratamako — from glutinous rice; for soft, smooth dango
- もち{粉|こ}: mochi flour — from glutinous rice; for soft mochi
- {団子粉|だんごこ}: dango flour — usually a blend of {上新粉|じょうしんこ} and {白玉粉|しらたまこ}
- {道明寺粉|どうみょうじこ}: coarse glutinous rice flour for sakura-mochi
